title: SS 1: Trading in Currencies — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Sets the Shariah rules for exchanging one currency for another.

title: SS 2: Debit Card, Charge Card and Credit Card — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Superseded by SS 61. This file is kept as a historical pointer only.

title: SS 3: Procrastinating Debtor — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Forbids charging extra money when a debtor pays late, and sets what creditors may do instead.

title: SS 4: Settlement of Debts by Set-Off — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Two ways people who owe each other can cancel out their debts: by agreement, or automatically when the conditions are met.

title: SS 5: Guarantees — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Sets the Shariah rules for guarantees that protect debts against delay and default.

title: SS 6: Conversion of a Conventional Bank to an Islamic Bank — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Lays out how a conventional bank converts into a fully Shariah-compliant bank.

title: SS 7: Hawalah — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Sets the Shariah rules for transferring a debt from one debtor to another.

title: SS 8: Murabaha to the Purchase Orderer — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Sets the Shariah rules for the bank's most-used financing: buy an asset, then resell it to the customer at a disclosed markup.

title: SS 9: Ijarah and Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Sets the Shariah rules for Islamic leasing, including leases that end with the customer owning the asset.

title: SS 10: Salam and Parallel Salam — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Sets the Shariah rules for paying in full now for goods to be delivered later.

title: SS 11: Istisna'a and Parallel Istisna'a — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Sets the Shariah rules for ordering something to be manufactured or built for future delivery.

title: SS 12: Sharikah (Musharaka) and Modern Corporations — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Sets the Shariah rules for partnerships — including modern companies and diminishing partnerships.

title: SS 13: Mudaraba — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Sets the Shariah rules for trustee partnerships: one side provides the money, the other provides the work.

title: SS 14: Documentary Credit — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Sets the Shariah rules for letters of credit used in trade.

title: SS 15: Ju'ala — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Sets the Shariah rules for reward-for-result contracts, where the work itself cannot be precisely defined.

title: SS 16: Commercial Papers — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Sets the Shariah rules for dealing in cheques, bills of exchange, and promissory notes.

title: SS 17: Investment Sukuk — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Sets the rules for sukuk — investment certificates that give holders ownership shares in real assets, projects, or services instead of paying interest.

title: SS 18: Possession (Qabd) — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Defines what counts as taking possession of something in a contract, including modern forms like holding the title documents.

title: SS 19: Loan (Qard) — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Sets the rules for loans, chiefly that no extra benefit may be demanded from the borrower, since that would be riba (interest).

title: SS 20: Sale of Commodities in Organised Markets — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Rules out futures, options, and similar speculative derivatives on organized exchanges, allowing only genuine trade in real commodities.

title: SS 21: Financial Paper (Shares and Bonds) — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Shariah rules for buying, holding and trading shares and bonds.

title: SS 22: Concession Contracts — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Rules for long-term deals where a company builds and runs a project, then hands it back — like a toll highway.

title: SS 23: Agency and the Act of an Uncommissioned Agent (Fodooli) — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Shariah rules for agency contracts and for acts done by someone who intervenes without being appointed.

title: SS 24: Syndicated Financing — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Shariah rules for large financing provided jointly by a group of financial institutions.

title: SS 25: Combination of Contracts — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Sets the rules for building one deal out of two or more contracts while keeping the whole structure compliant with Islamic law.

title: SS 26: Islamic Insurance — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Defines Islamic insurance (takaful) as donation-based mutual protection and sets the controls Islamic financial institutions must follow when offering it.

title: SS 27: Indices — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Sets the rules for building Shariah-compliant stock market indices and forbids buying or selling the index itself, which counts as gambling.

title: SS 28: Banking Services in Islamic Banks — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: States that Islamic banks may offer everyday banking services and charge fees for them, as long as the services do not involve interest-based lending.

title: SS 29: Stipulations and Ethics of Fatwa in the Institutional Framework — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Rules for how Islamic banks obtain religious rulings from their Shariah scholars, and the ethics those scholars must follow when issuing them.

title: SS 30: Monetization (Tawarruq) — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Strict conditions for tawarruq, a way of raising cash by buying a commodity on credit and selling it to a third party.

title: SS 31: Controls on Gharar in Financial Transactions — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Defines gharar (excessive uncertainty): which kinds of uncertainty break a contract and which kinds do not.

title: SS 32: Arbitration — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: How arbitration works for Islamic financial institutions: what can be arbitrated, who may serve as arbitrator, and how the verdict is issued and enforced.

title: SS 33: Waqf — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Superseded by SS 60. This file is kept as a historical pointer only.

title: SS 34: Hiring of Persons — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Rules for hiring people — employment and service contracts — under Islamic law.

title: SS 35: Zakah — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: How Islamic banks and companies calculate and pay zakah on their wealth.

title: SS 36: Impact of Contingent Incidents on Commitments — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: What happens to a contract when an unexpected disaster or event outside anyone's control disrupts it.

title: SS 37: Credit Agreement — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Rules for credit agreements between Islamic banks and their clients, including master agreements for future deals.

title: SS 38: Online Financial Dealings — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Rules for making Islamic financial contracts over the internet and other online channels.

title: SS 39: Mortgage and its Contemporary Applications — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Rules for mortgages — pledging an asset to secure a debt — and how they work in modern Islamic banking.

title: SS 40: Distribution of Profit in Mudarabah-based Investment Accounts — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Rules for how Islamic banks share profits with the holders of mudarabah-based investment accounts.

title: SS 41: Islamic Reinsurance — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Rules for retakaful — Islamic reinsurance, where takaful companies share large risks with each other.

title: SS 42: Financial Rights and How They Are Exercised and Transferred — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: The different kinds of financial rights — like ownership, usage rights, and easements — and how each may be used or passed on.

title: SS 43: Insolvency — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Islamic rules for when a debtor cannot pay — how insolvency is declared and how creditors are treated.

title: SS 44: Obtaining and Deploying Liquidity — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: The Shariah-compliant ways Islamic banks can raise cash when short and put spare cash to work.

title: SS 45: Protection of Capital and Investments — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Which methods of protecting invested capital are allowed in Islamic partnerships — and which are not.

title: SS 46: Al-Wakalah Bi Al-Istithmar (Investment Agency) — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Rules for investment agency — where you appoint someone to invest your money for a fee.

title: SS 47: Rules for Calculating Profit in Financial Transactions — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Rules for how Islamic banks calculate, present, and disclose profit in their financing and investment deals.

title: SS 48: Options to Terminate Due to Breach of Trust (Trust-Based Options) — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Gives a buyer the right to cancel a purchase when the seller lied, hid the truth, or charged far too much.

title: SS 49: Unilateral and Bilateral Promise — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: When a promise to do a deal in the future is only a moral duty and when a court can enforce it.

title: SS 50: Irrigation Partnership (Musaqat) — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Rules for a partnership where one person provides fruit trees and another person waters and cares for them, sharing the harvest.

title: SS 51: Options to Revoke Contracts Due to Incomplete Performance — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Gives buyers the right to cancel or get compensation when goods arrive faulty, incomplete, or not as described.

title: SS 52: Options to Reconsider (Cooling-Off Options, Either-Or Options, Revoke for Non-Payment) — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Rules for three options: thinking time after signing, canceling when the buyer does not pay, and picking one item from a list.

title: SS 53: Arboun (Earnest Money) — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Rules for earnest money: a deposit a buyer pays to hold a deal, which he loses if he walks away.

title: SS 54: Revocation of Contracts by Exercise of a Cooling-Off Option — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: How a contract can be canceled when the parties agreed in advance that one of them may revoke it.

title: SS 55: Competitions and Prizes — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Islamic rules for competitions, prizes, and promotional draws run or sponsored by financial institutions.

title: SS 56: Liability of Investment Manager — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: When a person managing someone else's investments must pay for losses: only for misconduct, negligence, or breaking the agreed terms.

title: SS 57: Gold and its Trading Parameters in Shari'ah — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Islamic rules for buying, selling, and investing in gold.

title: SS 58: Repurchase Agreement / Buyback — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Rules for buyback deals, where a seller sells an asset and later buys it back, and blocks structures that disguise interest.

title: SS 59: Sale of Debt — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Strict rules for selling debts, banning the sale of money-debts at a discount because that is interest.

title: SS 60: Waqf — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Rules for waqf, the Islamic endowment where an asset is locked in and its benefits given to charity, and it updates the earlier waqf standard.

title: SS 61: Payment Cards — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: Islamic rules for debit, prepaid, charge, and credit cards, banning interest-based revolving credit.

title: SS 62: Sukuk (exposure draft) — AAOIFI in Simple English
excerpt: This is a draft standard that would require sukuk to involve a genuine transfer of asset ownership to investors, replacing the current sukuk standard.
